title: Add ability to paste Klipper's contents on selection
line: With a new Clipboard option, picking a text entry from the clipboard history pastes it straight into the window you were typing in.
explanation: Choosing an entry in the clipboard popup only put it on the clipboard, so it still had to be pasted by hand; Wayland gives other apps no way to paste into the focused window, and faking Ctrl+V was rejected as a hack. KWin already had a clean path for injected text (InputMethod::sendText, used for libei text): it commits through text-input, or types the text as key events for clients without it. But a client that just got focus back drops text committed before it has handled the focus change. KWin now exposes insertText() on org.kde.KWin and holds text sent right after a focus change until the client updates its text-input state (500 ms at most). Klipper gets a 'Paste the selected entry into the active window' option (off by default, Wayland only): after a text entry is chosen and the popup closes, it waits for a Wayland round trip so KWin has handed the focus back, then calls insertText().

commits.message:
Add a D-Bus method to insert text into the focused window

Clipboard managers had no way to paste a chosen entry into the window
they were opened from. insertText() commits text through text input, and
text sent just after a focus change waits for the client to catch up.

BUG: 427214

klipper: optionally paste the selected entry into the active window

Choosing an entry only put it on the clipboard, so it still had to be
pasted by hand. A new option inserts text entries into the window that
gets the focus back once the popup closes, through KWin's insertText().

BUG: 427214

media.caption: Master: picking an older entry from the Meta+V popup only copies it; nothing appears in the editor
Patched, option on: picking the entry inserts it at the cursor
Patched: new 'Paste the selected entry into the active window' option (off by default)
